html:
An essential tool for long-duration astrophotography with an imprecise mount is the guide camera.

The guide camera is a camera that, mounted in parallel on the telescope, watches the movement of a star and sends the telescope mount movement instructions so that the star stays well centered. The goal is to correct the imperfect tracking or alignment of the mount during long photographic exposures.

There are several kinds of guide camera. The one I use is a QHY5 coupled to a 170 mm focal length finder and marketed by KWtelescope of Kitchener, Ontario.

For now, I have used it to guide the lx200 while shooting with the Takahashi Sky90 refractor at 407mm focal length. The stars are nicely round. The next photo session will be with the lx200 at a focal length of 1000mm. I will update this entry with the results.
